name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years, from the arrival of the first vanguard to pushing the defenders back to their mightiest cities. A dark future hangs over the Iron Kingdoms—will you stand firm against the invasion, or will you join it and revel in the spoils of war?

name: Name
body: Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons, with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios. When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player will choose to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games of the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible. Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Over the course of the campaign, players will track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles. Each player will be responsible to keep a tally of their own War Chest points. At the end of the third chapter, a player’s War Chest total will be used to rate that player’s performance as either an Invader of the Iron Kingdoms or as one of its valiant Defenders. War Chest points are awarded as follows: -Playing a Campaign Game: 1 point -Winning a Key Battle: +1 point -Winning by Killing the Opposing Leader: +1 point -Winning by Scenario Victory Conditions: +2 points

name: Name
body: Black Tide campaign scenarios are intended to be played in order. Each scenario grants the winning player, either the Invader or the Defender, an advantage in the subsequent scenario. Advantages are one-use only and can only be used the first time the winning player plays the scenario that follows the scenario in which the advantage was awarded.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Due to the nature of these scenarios, with the Invader sometimes striking the Defender without warning from sea or under the cover of darkness, the Invading player will not be allowed to place Defenses in same cases. It will be noted in the Terrain Placement section of each scenario whether the Invader can place Defenses or not.

name: Name
body: A flag is a scenario marker on a 40 mm base. A flag, however, is not a model. Models cannot end their movement on flags or be placed on them for any reason. A model can move through a flag if it has enough movement to move completely past it. While playing a Black Tide scenario, a player controls a flag when one or more of non-Cohort models are B2B with the flag and none of their opponent’s models contest it. A flag is contested if one or more of your opponent’s models are within 4" of it. Inert warjacks and wild warbeasts cannot contest flags.

name: Name
body: Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle gains an additional War Chest point.

name: Name
body:
<i>Smoke. Bitter smoke.
The cigar tasted foul in Lev’s mouth. He plucked it from between his teeth and curled his lip at the stub of rolled leaves, resting his foot on a jagged rock in the bottom of his hastily dug emplacement.
Perhaps it wasn’t the cigar; perhaps the day itself was too foul for his taste. It was stale and quiet, without banter or shouts or prayers from his men. The silence itself was oppressive.
Lev hated silence. He knew when the silence ended, the dying began.
On the distant horizon, a red flare sailed skyward.
Lev drew a long breath through his cigar, nodding once as if to acknowledge the brave spotter far ahead. He growled rather than raise his voice—he couldn’t shout the way he had when he was a young lieutenant. "All banners, two round volleys."
His adjutant, a cadet far too young to be facing the enemy in the field already, turned and yelled the command down the staggered line of artillery, their barrels raised as if in salute to the distant enemy. "All banners! Two round volleys!" The call was echoed in turn by each weapon crew as they sprang into action, pushing shells into place and slamming breeches closed.

name: Name
body: Lev’s voice was a low rumble, clouded by smoke. "Set ranges, five miles." "Range! Five miles!" His old armsmaster would have scolded him for not firing marking rounds first and made him run the length of the training yard with a shell in his arms. But they could not spare a single shot that did not shed invaders’ blood. They had to make the enemy stare into the fire and smoke and exhaust them before they reached Khadoran lines. There was no one else to stop the enemy if they could not. The horizon rippled. A row of tiny specks from this distance, growing and spreading across the distant hilltops like insects. Hundreds of them, thousands of them. An army, dragged from the ocean and marched a thousand miles to spit their curses at Lev Vaslov and his city. They would have to listen to his guns speak first. Lev blew a final wisp of smoke from his lips and stabbed the cigar out in the mud in front of him. "Blow them back to the sea." His adjutant’s hand slashed through the air. "All banners, fire!"

name: Name
body: Black Tide—Season 1, Chapter 3 is made up of three scenarios that should be played in order: "Counterattack," "Target of Opportunity," and "At the Gates."

name: Name
body: Hubris is the poison that rots the heart of the conqueror, and the invaders have pushed far and spread their forces thin. Behind their front lines, their supply caches lay vulnerable, waiting for the daredevil with the right mixture of courage and foolishness to steal in after them.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the Defender attacks the Invader’s camp to burn their supplies in a daring counterattack while the Invader rallies their forces from sleep to defend their caches.

name: Name
body: Scenario 7 is suitable for 50-point armies.

name: Name
body:
The Invader places six tents completely within 15" of the center of the table. The tents can be represented using available terrain and are suggested as 3"x5" each. The tents are treated as obstructions. The players then take turns, beginning with the Defender, placing five 50 mm objective markers within 10" of the center of the board and at least 3" from each other. These represent the supply caches.
The Defender is the first player when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. Neither player may play the Defenses Command Card when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: -To the Torch: A Defender model can destroy a supply cache if it begins its activation in base contact with the cache by making a special action. Remove destroyed caches from the board. -Standing Watch: When the Invader deploys their forces at the start of the game, they can only deploy up to half of their army’s points value. The Invader’s Leader model must also be placed during deployment. -Wake Up!: At the beginning of the Invader’s second turn, roll a die for each model/unit that has not been deployed. On a 3 or higher that model/unit is deployed in base contact with a randomly determined tent. At the beginning of the Invader’s third turn, all models/units not deployed on the first two turns are deployed in contact with randomly determined tent markers.

name: Name
body:
When a model/unit is deployed, if there is not room for a model to be deployed in base contact with the tent, remove that model from play.
Models/units deployed by Wake Up! activate normally the turn they are deployed.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if that player controls the only Leader model in play. (The winning player gains +1 War Chest point.)
The Defender wins when four or more objectives have been burned. (The winning player gains +2 War Chest points.)
The Invader wins if fewer than four objectives have been burned by the end of the Defender’s sixth turn. (The winning player gains +2 War Chest points.)

name: Name
body:
If the Invader player wins this match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #8: Target of Opportunity, that player can choose one unit to gain Prey.
Prey: After deployment but before the first player’s turn, choose an enemy model/unit to be this model/unit’s prey. This model gains +2 to attack and damage rolls against its prey. When the prey is destroyed ore removed from play, choose another model to be the prey.
If the Defender player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #8: Target of Opportunity, that player can choose up to two solos to gain Steady.
Steady: This model cannot be knocked down.

name: Name
body: In the haste of retreat, a commander finds themselves cut off from friendly forces, accompanied only by their personal guard, as war horns and the sound of racing feet surround them. The loyal defenders brace themselves back to back as the hilltops swarm with the invaders’ vanguard, encircling them like vultures and diving in to seize their prey.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the surrounded Defenders must survive and protect their Leader against endless waves of Invaders.

name: Name
body: Scenario 8 is suitable for 50 and 75-point armies.

name: Name
body:
The Defender’s deployment zone is a 15" diameter area in the center of the table. The Invader’s deployment zone extends 6" from the back of each table edge.
The Invader is the first player when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. Neither player may play the Defenses Command Card when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: Stand and Fight!: Defender warrior models in base contact with the Defender Leader gain Tough. Defender units with any model within 6" of the Defender Leader gain Battle-Driven. Battle-Driven: When one or more models in this unit are damaged by an enemy attack, after the attack is resolved models in this unit gain +2 ARM, +2 to their melee attack rolls and Pathfinder for one round. They’re Everywhere!: At the beginning of each Invader turn, the Invader can return any completely destroyed friendly non-Leader, non-Cohort model/unit back into play. Returned models/units must be placed completely within the Invader’s deployment zone. Returned models/units must forfeit their Combat Action the turn they are returned to play.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if that player controls the only Leader model in play. (The winning player gains +1 War Chest point.)
The Defender wins the match if that player’s Leader model is still in play at the end of the sixth turn. (The winning player gains +2 War Chest points.)

name: Name
body:
-If the Invader player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #9: At the Gates, that player can place two additional cover points during setup.
-If the Defender player wins the match, when playing the next scenario, Scenario #9: At the Gates, that player can place one additional cannon token during setup.

name: Name
body: The enemy waits with torch and ladder and ram. The defenders wait with cannon and sword and wall. There is no more time for fear, no more time for hesitation or doubt. It will all be decided here: if the waves from the sea will break upon the rocks, or if the battering will tear them down to their foundation.

name: Name
body: In this scenario, the Invader forces advance on the Defender’s city with siege weapons, stealing cover from the Defender’s artillery while they try to break through the gate and into the city itself.

name: Name
body: Scenario 9 is intended for 50-, 75-, and 100-point games

name: Name
body:
The Defender’s deployment zone extends 16" in from the rear of their table edge, and the front edge of this zone represents the city wall. The center 12" of the wall represents the City Gate.  The City Wall and City Gate are obstructions that grant cover. In the absence of terrain that will represent the wall, consider using dice spaced out along the line, as long as the position of the gate is clearly marked.  Place four 40mm objectives as shown by the red triangles on the map below.
After terrain is setup, the Defender places two 50 mm tokens along the city wall. These represent the cannons. The Invader then places three 50 mm markers on the board at least 8" from the Defender’s deployment zone. These represent the cover points.
The Invader is the first player when playing this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing other terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features.

name: Name
body: -The City Walls: Defender models in base contact with the city wall are considered to be on top of the wall and have elevation. Line of sight to and from models on top of the wall is not blocked by the wall. -The City Gate: The City Gate has DEF 5, ARM 22, and 20 damage boxes. The City Gate can be targeted by ranged and melee attacks. While there are no Invader models within 8" of the City Gate, Defender models treat it as open terrain. If the City Gate is destroyed, it is treated as open terrain by all models. -Artillery: At the start of the Defender’s turn, the Defender can attack with any of their available cannons targeting an enemy model. Cannons are RAT 4, RNG 20, AOE 3, and POW 14/8. Place a token by the cannon to indicate it has fired this turn. After a cannon has fired, it cannot fire the following turn while its crew reloads. -Cover Points: While within 4" of a cover point, models gain +2 DEF against ranged attacks and Resistance: Blast. -Siege Weapons: The Invader can assign two Battering Ram tokens and four Ladder tokens to their models after deployment. If a model with a token assigned to it is destroyed, that token is removed from play.

name: Name
body: -Battering Ram: Battering ram tokens can be given to units or Cohort models. The City Gate suffers –4 ARM against melee attacks from a model/unit with a battering ram token. -Ladders: Ladder tokens can be given to units or solos with a base size of 40 mm or smaller. A model/unit with a ladder token treats the City Wall as rough terrain instead of difficult terrain.

name: Name
body:
Starting on the second player’s second turn, at the end of each player’s turn, the Defender player scores 1 Control Point (CP) for each objective that player controls on their side of the City Wall and 3 CP for each objective they control on the Invader’s side of the City Wall. Simultaneously, the Invader scores 1 CP for each objective that player controls on their side of the City Wall and 3 CP for each objective they control on the Defender’s side of the City Wall.
If the City Gate is destroyed, the Invader scores 2 CP.

name: Name
body:
Each player gains 1 War Chest point for playing the match.
A player immediately wins the match if that player controls the only Leader model in play. (The winning player gains +2 War Chest point.)
At the end of the sixth turn, the player with the most CP wins. (The winning player gains +3 War Chest points.)

name: Name
body:
With the haze of recent battles still blanketing the Iron Kingdoms, the campaign season comes to an end. As you tally up the sum of your conquests, you may find your War Chest overflowing from your victories, or you may find it contains less bounty than defeat. Whatever the outcome, every experience only strengthens your armor and sharpens your sword for the battles ahead.
Below are the outcomes of the first campaign season, based on your final War Chest totals.

name: Name
body: The invasion has crashed against your army like the sea breaks against stones, and still you stand tall. The ones who would make your lands theirs lie scattered over that land in broken heaps and huddled camps. Their arrogance was their undoing, and your fortitude has proven to be stronger. Your banners, high above city walls littered with burns and cracks from siege engines, are a beacon of hope and a message to all who would challenge you: you will not be broken.

name: Name
body: The invaders have ground to a halt, and you have paid the price in blood to hold them at bay. The fields are torn by war and littered with the dead, and the specter of death wanders in gun smoke across the blasted landscape. Tomorrow, the sun will rise on broken cities and a wounded people. But they will be your cities and your people, and no enemy will take them from you.

name: Name
body: The banners of the enemy now fly over stone walls that were once yours, and their rulers claim the blood-soaked ground to be their own, yet you endure. In the hidden alleyways of cities and in the darkness of the forests, your forces hide, gather, and rebuild. Banners are but wood and cloth and the usurpers only flesh and blood. They can all be torn down in time.

name: Name
body: Your flags now fly over the enemy’s cities, and through surrender or bloodshed, their lands must admit to your rule. From the broken coast to the stone citadels, your army has marched and conquered mile after mile, and the time has come to bask in the spoils of war. When the smoke clears and the last pockets of resistance are dealt with, the only certainty is that this land, which defied you with such venom, is unquestionably now yours.

name: Name
body: Behind you drifts the smoke of ruin, and ahead is the smoke of guns from the waiting enemy. They know your banners now, and they tremble at the sight. They know your armies and your name, and they cannot help but know bloody chapter you have written into their histories. While many cities still stand ahead, and many miles have yet to be conquered, it is too late for them. You have your sword sunk deeply into this land, and you will not be moved from it now.

name: Name
body: Through gritted teeth and force of will, you still cling to this land. Your forces have dispersed, melting into the countryside and striking in raids and skirmishes: an army of robbers and bandits, yet still an army. The enemy will never fully know rest while you remain alive, and by the gods, devils, and upon your blades, you will see their flag torn down one day.
